T1.statement: Across G2-G4, T1 is dominated by persistence of unresolved/invalid process states after one local process-state revision.

T2.statement: T2 repeatedly produces route redirection without clean closure, regeneration, and fail-closed no-effect boundaries.

T3.statement: At the group-level response distribution, G2, G3 and G4 each contain one targeted suppression, one targeted redirection, one mixed effect and one persistence result; system identity within the middle categories is not identical across every group.

engineering_findings: Locality and efficacy remain empirically separable: all 34 valid paired interventions preserved unrelated structure while downstream effects were heterogeneous.
One-shot local process-state repair does not imply closure; persistence and mixed effects remain common descriptive outcomes in the frozen paired sample.
Regeneration is reproduced in each of G2, G3 and G4, supporting repair-generated process expansion as an observed engineering phenomenon rather than a single-group anomaly.
Fail-closed no-effect boundaries recur in G2 and G4 and are preserved outside the paired-effect denominator instead of being retried into a preferred outcome.
T1/T2/T3 show distinct recurring response geometries that should remain explicit in the final G2-G5 engineering synthesis.
